symptom.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the major depressive episode

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by a major depressive episode accompanied by hallucinations and/or delusions that are typically mood-congruent (e.g., themes of guilt, worthlessness, or deserved punishment). The psychotic features occur only during the depressive episode and do not persist independently, helping distinguish it from primary psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. Clinically, it often presents with pronounced functional impairment, high levels of distress, and an elevated risk of suicide, and may have a more severe and recurrent course than non-psychotic depression. Careful assessment of the temporal relationship between mood symptoms and psychosis, as well as exclusion of substance- or medical-induced causes, is crucial for accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.

patient.personality: Kip is a cautious, methodical retiree who channels his worry into careful planning, steady routines, and community involvement.
patient.stressor: Roughly half a year before seeking help, Kip was diagnosed with congestive heart failure after a brief hospitalization for shortness of breath, which forced him to confront his mortality and scale back his cherished mentoring, gardening, and volunteer commitments. Used to feeling in control of risk and contingencies, he struggled with the unpredictability of his health, frequent medical appointments, and the loss of his previous stamina, leading him to decline invitations to serve on boards and to stop his regular hikes. As the months passed, he spent more time alone at home reviewing his finances and family genealogy, ruminating on whether he had truly provided for his children and what legacy he would leave, and he gradually withdrew from church and the food bank, which had previously anchored his weeks. His primary care physician became concerned when Kip mentioned that he was increasingly preoccupied with the idea that his life might already be effectively “over” and that he had started wondering whether it would be better to bring things to a close on his own terms, prompting an urgent psychiatric referral.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I keep thinking about how I might be better off dead and wondering if there’s any point in going on like this.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: More and more, especially in the evenings when the house is quiet, I hear this low, distinct voice right behind my left ear telling me things like, “You’ve ruined your family’s future,” or, “They’d be better off if you were gone,” and it sounds so real that I catch myself turning my head to answer it even though I know no one is there.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days now I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like a curtain has been pulled down over everything, and I just lie there thinking, “This is it, this is all my life is going to be from now on,” and it feels completely hopeless no matter what I try to tell myself logically.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to look forward to tending my tomatoes or meeting the young folks I mentored, but these past months I just stare at the garden from the kitchen window and let the weeds take over, and when people call to ask me to help with a project or come to church, I make excuses because the idea of going or caring about any of it feels pointless and exhausting.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My wife keeps asking if I’m alright because I either sit in the same chair for long stretches, barely moving and struggling to get the words out when she talks to me, or I’m shuffling aimlessly from room to room, wringing my hands and straightening already straight piles of papers, too agitated to sit but too slowed down to actually do anything useful.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I’ve done almost nothing but sit and read the mail, I feel like I’ve run a marathon—just walking from the bedroom to the kitchen leaves me so drained that I have to lean on the counter and catch my breath, and the thought of taking a shower or driving to the store feels like climbing a mountain I don’t have the strength for anymore.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I can’t shake the conviction that I’ve failed my family—that by getting sick I’ve somehow squandered all the years of careful planning, and I lie awake replaying every financial decision and even small mistakes from decades ago, convinced that any hardship my kids or grandkids ever face will be because I was careless and selfish and deserve to be punished for it.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: For months now, almost every night when I’m lying there staring at the ceiling, I find myself thinking very calmly that it might be better for everyone if I just weren’t here anymore, and I’ve gone so far as to work out in my head exactly how I could use the pills in the medicine cabinet so that my wife would find me “peacefully” and finally be free of the burden I’ve become.
